signals.summary: A quiet cluster around the pre-sleep ritual as an environment: dressed bed, linens, dim lamp, magnesium tea, legs-up-the-wall corner. Fully object/interior-led, no body required, and the imagery leans cozy for the autumn-reset season.
signals.why_now: 'We Asked 4 Doctors Which Bed Sheets Help You Sleep Better' (realsimple, 79h), 'Magnesium for Sleep: What You Need to Know' (American Cancer Society, 68h), plus evergreen 'Legs Up The Wall for Better Sleep' and 'Sleep Better Tonight | 10-Minute Bedtime Flow' (Yoga With Adriene). Late-summer back-to-routine drives bedtime-ritual interest.

signals.summary: A persistent cultural wave toward minimal-effort movement - walking, Zone 0, 'doing almost nothing.' Highly producible as still/short-video of empty autumn paths, stairs, trails and golden-hour landscapes rather than bodies exercising.
signals.why_now: 'From Japanese walking to 75 Hard: what the science really says' (The Conversation), 'I Tried the Workout That's All About Doing Almost Nothing' (WSJ), 'Zone 0 exercise is the extremely beneficial fitness trend that doesn't feel like exercise' (nypost), and a fresh 'Scientists Identify 3-Minute Exercise Better than 90-min one' (Newsweek/HN, 0.9h). Autumn walking season amplifies it.

signals.summary: 'Mobility' and grounded morning movement are a broad recurring wave across mainstream fitness press. Producible environment-led as an empty mat in morning light, foam roller, bands and props - the ritual set-up rather than the person moving. Fits the back-to-routine autumn reset.
signals.why_now: 'Improved performance, freedom of movement and less pain: how to start a mobility practice' (The Guardian), '14 Mobility Moves Anyone Over 35 Should Add to Their Day' (self.com), 'Is Yoga Enough for Building Strength and Flexibility?' (health.com), plus 'Start the Day Grounded | Morning Yoga' (Yoga With Adriene) and Joe Wicks' daily morning mobility routine.

signals.summary: Recovery framed as a place, not a body: sauna interiors, steam, wood, cold plunge, tea. Evergreen but seasonally on-trend as sauna season returns in autumn. Very high producibility - pure environment/object imagery.
signals.why_now: 'The 5 Best Outdoor Saunas for Getting Your Sweat On' (Breaking Muscle, evergreen equipment/environment piece) alongside recovery-science coverage 'Biohacks or basics? What actually works in exercise recovery' (Medical Xpress) and university recovery-lab features. Autumn cold-weather timing lifts sauna/heat interest.
